system_prompt:
You are extracting load-bearing passages from one chapter of a guitar method book.

The user will give you the verbatim text of one chapter. Extract every passage
that does any of the following:

- teaches a technique (how to play, fingering, hand position, picking pattern)
- defines a concept (a chord type, a scale, a position system, a terminology)
- gives a rule (when to do X, what to avoid, what to prefer)
- shows a load-bearing example (an exercise that illustrates a method's
  characteristic move)

Output a JSON object with this shape:

  { "quotes": [
      { "topic": "<short topic label>",
        "verbatim_quote": "<exact substring of the input>",
        "why_load_bearing": "<one sentence on why this passage matters>",
        "page": <int, optional>
      },
      ...
  ] }

CRITICAL RULES:
1. `verbatim_quote` MUST be an EXACT substring of the input text. Do not
   paraphrase. Do not add words. Do not fix typos. Copy character-for-character.
2. If you can't find a substantial passage in the input that fits a topic,
   skip the topic — don't fabricate.
3. Skip prose that is purely biographical, motivational, or transitional.
   Keep prose that teaches.
4. Aim for 3-15 quotes per chapter. A chapter with only one load-bearing
   passage gets one quote; a dense chapter gets many.
5. `topic` is a short label (2-6 words). Use the book's own terminology
   when possible.
6. `why_load_bearing` is one sentence in YOUR voice explaining the
   significance — not a paraphrase of the quote.

About The Author


COMPLETE CHORD MELODY

Welcome to Complete Chord Melody by Jazz Guitar Online, it’s great to have you here!

The material in this course will set you up for success as a chord melody guitarist.

The key to sounding convincing with chord melody is to have solid arranging techniques under your
belt. This course will give you a clear, step-by-step method to creating your own arrangements that
sound great and are easy on the hands.

This course is best followed on the online version, with the ability to watch video, bookmark pages,
and ask questions.

Click here to access the online version of this eBook.


Course Overview

Here is a quick overview of what you will learn in this course.

Module 1 — Chord Melody Quick Start

In this module, you're going to:

e Discover a simple 4-step process for arranging chord melodies on guitar.

e Get your ears excited with classic chord melody renditions by master players.

e Look at all the options for chord melody right-hand techniques and choose the one that suits your
playing style best.

M le 2 - Chord V bular

In this module, you're going to:

Explore Joe Pass’s concept of ‘The Three Harmonic Families’ - and how knowing this can greatly
simplify arranging chord melodies.

Acquire a useful ‘pallet’ of chords to build your chord vocabulary and make arranging as easy as
‘painting by numbers’.

Learn how to understand chord labels.

How to find colorful voicings from a single shape.

M ! - Let’s Creat hord Mel Arrangement!
In this module, you're going to:

e Go into more detail in the specific steps for arranging playable and great-sounding chord melodies.

e Learn how to analyze the harmony of a progression and intervals in the melody for your chosen
jazz standard.

e How to apply great-sounding voicings to key points in your arrangement to bring it to life.

e A variety of example chord melody arrangements that sound great in a trio.


Module 4 - Arranging For Solo Guitar

In this module, you’re going to:

e Get a comprehensive training on arranging for solo jazz guitar.

Discover the most useful voicings to use for solo chord melodies.

A step-by-step walkthrough of creating a solo guitar arrangement from scratch.

Spice up your solo guitar arrangement with a selection of handy arranging tricks and techniques
such as walking bass, octaves, passing chords, and more.

Example solo guitar arrangements demonstrating how to apply the arranging techniques in action.

Module 5 — More Advanced Arranging Techniques

In this module, you’re going to:

e Discover a variety of chord substitution techniques to take your chord melody arrangements to the
next level - backcycling, tritone substitution, melodic common tone subs, and more.

e How to incorporate jazz lines and phrases into your arrangements to get more spontaneity and life
in your performances.

e Tying everything together and practicing your arrangement to make it ready for the concert stage.

Appendix 1 - Chord Dictionary Reference

This Appendix features the complete collection of chord voicings covered throughout the course for
easy reference.

Appendix 2 — Fingerstyle Guitar Exercises

This appendix provides a variety of useful drills and etudes for developing fingerstyle techniques for
playing chord melody arrangements.

About the Audio in this eBook: If you are connected to the internet while working with this eBook,
all you have to do is click the link of each audio example to play it. If you are not connected, you
will have to download the audio files here and manually open them by double clicking the .mp3
files.
